claim: This chapter teaches that 'X is at Y' can be said with に あります／います or contracted to です, but only the grammar2 pair carries the hint that says which form is wanted, so the other location cards are a coin toss on Production.
evidence: Unhinted cards: ks4-smith-floor 'Smith-san is on the second floor.' -> ...にいます; fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin 'The florist is next to the hospital.' -> ...にあります; fib-tanakasan-doko-q 'Where is Tanaka-san?' -> どこにいますか; fib-tanakasan-doko-a 'He's in the president's office.' -> しゃちょうしつにいます. Each has an equally correct です form (chapter-13-extras sp-ima-doko-q: 'with a person, the place +です contraction works the same way it does for things'). Hinted cards: grammar2-2, grammar2-3.

verdictReason: All four cards verified unhinted (ks4-smith-floor, fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin, fib-tanakasan-doko-q, fib-tanakasan-doko-a), and GRAMMAR 2 ②/②' makes the です contraction equally correct for every は-topic location sentence (sp-ima-doko-q's note extends it to people). The shared rule "when one English shape maps to two structures, the hint names the structure" applies, and the deck already does this on grammar2-2/2-3. Fixer: hint only は-topic location statements and questions (が existence sentences have one form), and word it without quoting the ending where possible.

claim: The romaji line is written differently from card to card for the same words, which makes the 'Says' line look like it is teaching a distinction that does not exist.
evidence: fib-meishi-desk-count 'roku-mai' but nanmai card 'nanmai'; fib-fork-table-count-q 'nan-bon' but nanbon card 'nanbon'; fib-fork-table-count-a 'jup-pon'; fib-kumano-chikai-a 'nijup-pun ... Basu de'; fib-kumano-chikai-q 'Kumano-jinja' but kumanojinja card 'kumano jinja'; fib-tanakasan-doko-q 'Tanaka-san' but sorekara-example 'tanaka-san'. Preflight lists only mit-tsu and san-nin here.
fix: Normalise these to the deck's romaji style (no counter hyphens, one casing rule for names).
verdictReason: The inconsistencies are real but the proposed direction is partly backwards. Per the pinned style (src/translate/romajiStyle.js): number+counter hyphenates, so roku-mai, jup-pon and nijup-pun are RIGHT; proper nouns capitalise with a hyphenated suffix, so Tanaka-san and Kumano-jinja are RIGHT. The wrong ones here are nan-bon (なん is not a number; the deck has nanbon x2, nanmai x3, nannin), "Basu de" (mid-romanization capital on a common noun), the kumanojinja word card "kumano jinja", and sorekara-example "tanaka-san". Collection-wide: Tanaka-san 19 / tanaka-san 15 / tanaka san 14. Preflight lints only the counter and honorific hyphen, not casing or the apostrophe.

Note for the fixer: the script-quoting rule requires quoted kana in a hint to carry romaji AND an English gloss, so reword the gloss (e.g. "san, the softening suffix") rather than deleting it.

claim: The target writes 10ほん where the book's exercise prints the sound-changed 10 ぽん, which the rest of the deck follows.
evidence: Book, EXERCISES II A-2: "A : ( フォーク、なんぼん ) B : (10 ぽん )". Card target: "10ほんあります" (romaji jup-pon arimasu). Other cards spell the change: そのあかワインを１ぽんください, ビールを３ぼんください, バスで20ぷんぐらいです.

verdictReason: Book EXERCISES II A-2 prints 10 ぽん. The deck's own digit+kana targets spell the sound change (ビールを１ぽんとワインを２ほんください, ビールを３ぼんください, バスで20ぷんぐらいです, 30ぷん, 40ぷん), and the Lesson 5 ３ぼん note says so explicitly. On a kana deck the target IS the reading, and 10ほん tells the learner the counter is read ほん after 10, which is false; ttsText じゅっぽんあります and pronunciation jup-pon are already right, so only the target changes. Raised from polish because the front teaches a wrong reading.

verdictReason: Verified: ks1-chairs, ks2-guests and pen-drawer-example ship with no note, and no Lesson 13 note states the GRAMMAR 1 order "place に thing/person が number あります／います"; only the two たくさん notes mention the missing particle.
